If there are any inconsistencies or errors, please comment. The NATO OoB comprises 1 Type 205, 2 Type 206 submarines on the Baltic Sea, 1 Delfinin submarine on the North sea and 1 Dolfijn sub and an Atlantique MP on Amsterdam. 2 Tornados, 2 Phantoms and 1 Atlantique are stationed in Esbjerg. Finally, a German ship group on Kiel.  On the Soviet side, 2 Foxtrot and 2 Whiskey subs on the Baltic Sea, 3 Badger regiments, 1 Il-38 and 1 helicopters MP, 2 Foxbats, 2 Floggers on Baltic air bases. On the Baltic ports: 1 Victor II and Yankee SSN boats, The aicraft carrier Minsk with its air complement, the Kirov, 1 Sovremenny Udaloy, 1 Kresta and 1 Kynda fleet groups. Finally, 2 amphibious units. Soviet facilities are defended by a SAM unit.  Rolling for weather with scenario special rules. Roll 4, good weather on North 1-2.Start of turn 1:Start of the first turn.  Fast Task Forces may move.  TF Viking leaves Kiel’s port into the Baltic sea.  Soviets react with Port Watch event. Whiskey class submarine uses two dice to detect TF Viking. Rolls 1-2. No effect. Submarine is spent.Soviets play Port Watch.  Soviets launch an air strike against facilities in Germany with two Badgers. German Phantoms roll for CAP with 2 dice each and +1 of Tactical Value. Roll 2-5-7-8 for two hits. Badgers have a save roll on +6 for attacking a land installation. Roll 1-9, one step is destroyed. 12 missiles inbound. This translates to 2 dice of cruise missile against land targets. No modifiers apply. Roll 4-5 for two hits in total. Facility has light damage. Badgers are spent. Red 6 Ops remaining.Badgers first attack.  Ships may move. Badgers spent markers are removed.  NATO performs ASW on the Baltic sea with a Type 206 submarine. Roll 3-4-6-10. Attacker can allocate a N10 and does so to an enemy Foxtrot submarine. Type 206 is spent. Blue 5 Ops remaining.NATO ASW damages Soviet Foxtrot.  Soviets decided to not waste any more time. They form Task Force Andropov with a Yankee (SSN), Kresta group, Kynda group, Sov-Udaloy, Kirov, Minsk and two amphibious units. Red 4 Ops remaining.  NATO is hurrying repairs on the damaged facilities. Damage is reduced to 1. Blue 3 Ops remaining.  Ops track repairs are performed. German facility is fully repaired.  Soviets launches two regiments of Badgers again. Phantoms rolls for CAP, 1-3-4-5 +1 Tactical Value. No damage is inflicted to the strike units. 12 missiles incoming. Roll of 2 dice on cruise missiles to land targets 5-7 for two hits and a collateral damage allocated by NATO. One step destroyed on the Atlantique MP. Badgers are spent. Red 2 Ops remaining.  Task forces may move. TF Andropov moves first. Leaves port. TF Viking remains in position. TF Andropov uses its intrinsic MP assets to detect TF Viking. Rolls a 2 for no effect. Badgers spent markers are removed.  NATO launches the Atlantique on the dutch bases to detect TF Andropov. Minsk’s Forgers roll for MP disruption. They will disrupt on a 9+ and a step loss on a N10. Rolls a 7 for no effect. Atlantique rolls with one die for task force detection. Rolls 8 and TF Andropov is poorly detected. MP is spent. Blue 2 Ops remaining.Successful detection on TF Andropov.   After detection, NATO goes for the attack on the Task Force with a Type 206 submarine. Rolls 6-7-10-10 which can cause two hits on any target on the Task Force and one hit on a PM/Amph/Convoy. TF Andropov total TF ASW value is 16 which gives 4 dice with no modifiers to defend itself. Rolls 2-5-7-9. One attack N10 is stopped and causes a step loss on the NATO submarine. (Edit: as pointed out on the posts below, Task Forces can only cause step loss on a non-magnetic submarine with a N10. No step loss would have occurred in this case) NATO allocates one hit on the Kirov and the one of the amphibious units. Rolls 2 dice for capital ship damage on the Kirov with a 10-10. Kirov is sunk. The amphibious unit receive one hit. Type 206 is spent. There will be reckoning. Blue 1 Op remaining.Devastating attack of the Type 206 on TF Andropov.  Soviets launch an Il-38 to detect TF Viking. Rolls one die with a 4. TF Viking is poorly detected. Il-38 is spent. Red 1 Op remaining.TF Viking is now detected.  Immediately, one regiment of Badgers go for TF Viking, it is unopposed. 6 missiles incoming. The German group has 2 SAM available against them. Rolls 1-10, shooting down two missiles. 4 go through. Soviet rolls two dice for each two missiles on the incoming missile resolution with 5-8. 3 hits are caused. No need for allocation dice as the strike will destroy the whole Task Force. TF Viking is destroyed and the Badger is spent. Red is out of operation points.  NATO uses the Type 205 submarine to attack TF Andropov. Rolls 3-10 which grants a hit on any target selected by the attacker. Currently, TF Andropov has an ASW value of 14, which gives 4 dice with no modifiers to defend itself. Rolls 1-9-10-10. Stops the attack and causes three step losses on the attacker, completely destroying it. Blue is out of operation points.  End of turn 1. All the spent markers are removed and roll 10 for weather. Bad weather on the Baltic sea.Map overview at the end of the first turn.Start of turn 2:  Ops track repairs are conducted on the NATO facilities.  Soviets launch helicopters to perform ASW warfare on the Baltic. They roll 2 dice less due to bad weather Rolls 6-9 causing one step on step loss. NATO allocates the step on the two step Type 206. (Edit: as mentioned on the comments below, a MP can only cause a step loss on a non-magnetic submarine with a N10) The helicopter MP is spent. Red 7 Ops remaining.Retaliation on the Type 206 submarine with ASW helicopters.  Task Forces may move. TF Andropov is affected by the bad weather and the invasion is stalled.TF Andropov suffers from bad weather.  NATO uses the Dutch Atlantique to improve detection on TF Andropov. Minsk’s Forger rolls for disruption with 1. No effect. The MP rolls one die for a 3. Detection is improved on TF Andropov. MP is spent. Blue 5 Ops remaining.  NATO uses one Type 206 submarine to attack TF Andropov. The good detection and the bad weather modifiers cancel each other out. The attacker rolls 1-5-6 which provides a hit. TF Andropov has an ASW value of 12 that is modified for bad weather. The Task Force has 3 dice with no modifiers to defend itself. Rolls 1-3-7 for no effect. NATO allocates the hit on the Sov-Udaloy group. Type 206 submarine is spent. Blue 4 Ops remaining.  Soviets uses the Victor I submarine to perform ASW on the Baltic sea. The bad weather hampers the attack to one die. Rolls 4 for no effect. Victor I is spent. Red 6 Ops remaining.Bad weather ASW is pretty difficult for old boats.  NATO use a Type 206 submarine to attack TF Andropov. The good detection and the bad weather modifiers cancel each other out. The attacker rolls 6-6-9 which provides a two hits and a hit on a PM/Amph/Convoy. TF Andropov has an ASW value of 11	 that is modified for bad weather. The Task Force has 3 dice with no modifiers to defend itself. Rolls 2-4-9 which stops the die 9 and causes a step loss on the Type 206 submarine destroying it. (Edit: as pointed out on the posts below, Task Forces can only cause step loss on a non-magnetic submarine with a N10. No step loss would have occurred in this case) NATO allocates the hits remaining. Hits the remaining step of the Sov-Udaloy step and causes a step loss on the Kynda group. Blue 3 Ops remaining.Type 206 punching again TF Andropov again. Little time remains to hamper the invasion.  The Soviets launch two regiments of Badgers to the German facilities. Phantoms roll for cap with one die less each for light damage on their air base. Roll 3-7 with a +1 modifier. Badgers can save on a 6+ for attacking a land facility. Roll one. Badgers suffer one step loss. 12 Missiles incoming. Attacker roll 2 dice on the cruise missiles against land targets roll with a 6-7 with a -1 modifier for bad weather. Facility receives two hits for a total of 3 and its heavy damaged. Badgers are spent. Red 4 Ops remaining.Badgers just keep coming. The German air force has no chance to take off.  Repairs are performed on the German facilities leaving it light damaged.  NATO moves Delfinin submarine from The North sea to the Baltic sea. Delfinin is spent. Blue 2 Ops remaining.  Soviets use Foxtrot for ASW on the Baltic sea. Bad weather reduces the roll to one die. Rolls 7 for no effect. Foxtrot is spent. Red 3 Ops remaining.  Ship may now move. TF Andropov prepares for landing operations. They will start amphibious assault on the next ships turn. Badgers spent markers are removed. Soviet combines two one step Badgers regiments into a full regiment.Soviets are preparing for the assault. Any bets on Denmark?  NATO performs repairs on the German facilities. Damage is reduced to one hit. Blue is out of operation points remaining.  The Soviets launch two regiments of Badgers to the German facilities. tier2.author: Rick
tier2.body: Hi all,I'd like to solicit community opinion on two points regarding the Soviet surface fleet, and the NATO response to it.1) The Soviet Mediterranean squadron. What good is it?At the risk of sounding a bit dismissive, it seems pointless. I know why they kept it there in reality (tool of influence for peacetime incidents), but once the shooting war starts, it seems like a complete lame duck. It has very weak defences and will be sunk as soon as a US CVBG decides to take an interest; the offensive capabilities are similarly negligible, needing a card to fire off the white missiles in response.I'm really struggling to see why the Soviet player wouldn't just pull both units out in the pregame adjustment every time. Conversely I suppose you could reinforce it with a bonus 3 units... has anyone tried this, and if so how did it go?2) Stopping the early deathstar.In pregame deployment the Soviets can deploy one task force with ships from any one port, anywhere on the map.So shift the two Mediterranean units & the Kirov to the Kola Peninsula, then form a task force with everything there, an Alfa escort, and the starting amphibs. Pop your horrifying 20 ASW /18 SAM monster down either off Orland, or Reykyavik.You'll only need two Ship phases - or a single turn - to complete your landing. Meanwhile your amphibs are safely nestled inside a steel box of protection.Looking from NATO's side of the map - how can you stop this?In our recent game, I deployed slightly more conservatively and put the  deathstar off Bodo, moving it off Orland in the first Ships phase. The NATO player threw everything he had at it - Buccaneers bombing away, the two northern carriers rolling in, practically every submarine in the area thrown in, lucky card play eliminating the escort sub - and even then, while he sank practically my entire surface fleet, the amphibs still got through.If I'd given him one less Ship phase to react (and used an Alfa as the escort for the save) - I don't see how he could possibly have countered the landing. It's not even ops intensive for the Soviets! Commit some extra patrolling subs if you have them spare - but otherwise it will all happen automatically!Anyone have any bright ideas on how you'd resist that kind of early push?

tier2.author: Chris
tier2.body: 17.7.4 says, "Resolve exactly as for Fighter vs Fighter combat [emphasis added], but the non-striking player may roll with a number of fighters equal to the number of enemy Strike or Fighter units."  But since 17.6 says. "If both sides have fighters in the same Sea Zone the Soviet player must declare if he will avoid combat followed by the NATO player.  If either does so, return Interceptors to base 'Spent', and place a 'Spent' marker on CAP units.  They take no further part in this combat."  That means that one escorting Fighter step can choose to avoid combat and by so doing negate all defending CAP, leaving the Strike aircraft to attack unmolested.  This is absurd!Surely this is not what's intended, but what is?  And is it correct that when CAP is defending bases (and thus not technically in the attackers' Sea Zone), neither side may avoid combat?Our house rule is that if the escorting Fighters choose to avoid combat, only an equal number of CAP units become spent.  The Strike aircraft may continue their attack, but players must then use the 17.7 Fighter vs. Air Strike procedure against all remaining CAP Fighters, which may include some Spent units as a result of the abort.We hope that the whole Fighter vs. Escorted Air Strike procedure is fleshed out in much greater detail in the new Pacific volume.

Then you read reports and operator testimony...most of which reveal technology that was considerable less sophisticated in which the fancier features “didn’t work” or “never worked” or “didn’t even work in exercises.” (Dirty Little Secret: There was a fair amount of that on our side too and some systems that were supposed to be fielded “in a couple of years” when I was in are just maturing, just being field tested, or still a few years away 30 years later.)It’s like the MiG-25:  it’s made of titanium, it flies at 3 Mach and has a look-down/shoot-down radar! tier2.author: Boinky10
tier2.body: Please excuse the long post, with questions.  WRT Andersson's earlier question about whether CAP on English airbases protect the port in England....  I was quite confused by issues with terminology and want to confirm a few things:  Rule 17.3: "Land based fighters protect land bases in their zone." (1) Zone here means "Land zone," and not the "sea zone" that the airbase fronts onto?  I ask because 6.9 defines "land AREAS."  "Sea zones" are discussed in 6.2.  And the phrase "land ZONE" never appears in the rules anywhere.  Hence, I took this to mean that aircraft protect against attacks from "sea zones" that they front.  So, to add some more specifics to Andersson's original question, I take it (now) from the answer to his post that I was wrong and that CAP located on UK airbases can defend against bombers attacking from North 5-6?  (2) Similarly, a Soviet bomber (or TF) can launch a strike on UK airfield from North 5-6?  6.12 says "...when a facility is being attacked the attacking units only need to be able to reach an adjacent sea zone."  6.9 says "The airfield and port symbols are used to show which sea zones the facility is adjacent to.  Any symbol or airfield/port box touching a sea zone indicates adjacency."  If the answer to the question is "yes," bombers can launch from North 5-6, then there are two different definitions of adjacency, one for movement from an airbase / port and a different one for strikes against ports and airfields.  I would recommend clarifying all this in the next version of the rules.  I am not trying to be a literalist or to nitpick, but I usually assume that the language in a rulebook says what it says for a reason. But while I will confess to being frustrated with the rule book, I am extremely grateful to your willingness to field questions on BGG.  The game and design (if not the rulebook) are excellent, and the BGG Q&A makes it possible to play.  I have been accused in the past of being passive-aggressive, and this post will surely prove my friend correct in that assessment.  :-)  But I do love the game.  Best,Eric

tier2.author: WriterJWA
tier2.body: Stuart Tonge  @stuuk Hi jerad, rules sections will be rewritten. The rules are already cross referenced but happy to correct mistakes.Can you give an indication of one or more rules that have caused consternation? If some portions need moving or even repeating we can look at doing thatThanks for asking! That's really cool.I think it's a matter of getting relevant information grouped in way that builds on itself. For instance weather... In the 10.0 Determine Weather, the rules describe how weather is determined for each sea zone. Awesome, it's a cool system. However, there are not mentions of the weather's impact on movement or combat or any other function. That has to be sussed out by reading the charts or just mining the rules for references to weather (which points to my lack of cross-referencing rules, because there are none in 10.0). So it would be helpful to go to 10.0 Determine Weather (which could just be 10.0 Weather) and find every impact weather has on the game. Another example is 7.0 Determining Victory. We learn about victory conditions before we understand how the mechanisms work to achieve it. Now, I can see a point that suggests it would be helpful to understand the objective of the game overall, but that could be added in as a line or two up front, then expanded in the Victory section. But that section might be better served toward the end of the book. From an overall organizational standpoint, by advice there would be to develop the rules from general to specific. So instead of having Task Forces, Task Force Movement, Special Units & Concepts, Capital Ships, and Repairing Ships ahead of Operations Points, put the order from the basic game mechanic of operations to how they're applied in each case, and how they're modified or altered by the previously listed sections. The Operations mechanism is at the heart of the game engine; the player should know that before know how it's altered by unit types and other conditions. To that end, here's a possible outline as an example:IntroComponents--Units--Map--Cards--Charts--DiceUnits & StatusTurn SequenceOperations--How the operation system works.--How each unit moves by way of operations points.--Capital ships and Task Force creation (because these two are interlinked).--Task force movement. Combat--A basic explanation of the combat system.--A detailed by-type procedure of combat (like you have here, which works!).After that, get into things like Special Units & Concepts, Weather, and so on.

I have played this scenario once or twice already and have found that the Soviets tend to be successful when they start (and continue to) hammer the UK airfields. This time, however, I decided not to do that in order to help promote the kind of gameplay situations that I'm unsure about, especially air vs. air encounters. All in all I had a lot of fun playing it, even if the outcome felt very quick and lopsided this particular go through.  NATO Set-Up: NATO set up in three task forces (TFs). Two with two carriers each and a small third TF to both act as a bit of a decoy and to also engage in a little extra ASW. The two main TFs started in East 4 in order to eliminate the possibility of a first turn air strike by the Soviets. The small force started by the GUIK gap in East 6.Aegis: US-1, SturgeonHammer: Kitty Hawk, Saratoga US-2, 3, (fleets total 10 SAM, 7 ASW), SturgeonMustang: Kennedy, Nimitz, US-4, 5 (fleets total 9 SAM, 7ASW), Los AngelesIt was clear, placid day in the Northern corners of the world when all hell broke loose. Signals intelligence confirmed that four American carrier groups were en route to attack the Motherland's essential defensive assets on the Kola Peninsula. NATO, of course, immediately noticed Russia's move to a red alert standing but feeling that they still held a significant advantage decided to press on with the attack. Pre-Game Questions:1) I was a little confused by the 0-range fighters. Am I correct that they are for CAP only and can defend both the air base and the port?2) Is it correct that the Soviet ships in port do NOT begin in a TF?3) The SAM unit is simply located in "Kola." Is it correct that it can/will defend both the port and the air base?Turn 1In turn one each side sets their board before exchanging a pair of devastating strikes.Not wanting to play to many ops points before the first ships turns, the USSR begins by sending an MP OP in the Norwegian Sea. The Brits then put fighters on patrol In the same area. Q:Since the MP is already OP, there is no fighter vs. MP interaction at this time, correct?FAST MOVE: TF Aegis moves into the Norwegian Sea while the other two part ways. Hammer moves due East into the North Sea. TF Mustang sails to East 4. USSR MP unit declines to search, preferring to stay on patrol until after the ship step. RORSAT detects Aegis. Q:  Is it correct that the MP can decline to search and stay OP in the zone?Still not wanting the make a big move before the ships step, a Foxtrot attacks TF Aegis (6-9). Countermeasures prove ineffective, resulting in a step loss to US-1. A Los Angeles class sub rallies to Aegis' side, conducts ASW and, with an N10, causes a step loss to the Victor I unit. Q: Because a 9 vs a TF hits Prairie Masker, etc. according to the chart, is it correct that NATO must allocate the hit to a ship of that type and cannot just give it to the submarine?The Soviets now spend 2 ops to form a TF (all eligible ships). NATO puts a Nimrod on Patrol in the Barents Sea. SHIPS: TF Aegis attempts to hunt down those darn Soviet subs before they can cause havoc on the larger task forces (5-5-7). Alas, even their rocket torpedoes don't catch prey since 8, after all, is less than 9. Because of that attempt, however, TF Aegis retains their Poor Detection status. TF Gorshkov enters the Barents Sea. The patrolling Nimrod rolls for detection (scores Good)Q: In this case, the MP is NOT attacked prior to rolling for detectionHammer and Mustang both move in to N5-6, Hammer first. The patrolling Bear rolls upon Hammer's entry, scoring good detection. The RORSAT detects Mustang. Sensing an impending attack, the Soviets launch Mig Foxhounds to patrol the Barents Sea. Will they help? Now is the moment that NATO begins its offensive. A squad of Buccaneers launch from the UK, heading straight for the Kola penninsula, accompanied by an escort of F4 Phantoms. The MIGs intercept the strike package (6-7-8, +2 = 3 hits) The fighters are eliminated and the strike planes take a ste(e)p loss. Q: NATO fighters do not get to roll against the Foxhounds, yes?Q: At this point, NATO may abort the strike, yes?Deciding not to abort, the Buccaneer now faces Floggers flying CAP.  Because the strike was intercepted CAP gets an extra die for a total of 4 dice with a +1 tactical value. Rolls of 5-5-6-6 miss anyway. NATO allocates all dice to SEAD (3-9-0). 4 Hits on the SAMQ: Since the SAM has a max value of 3. Is it limited to 3 hits?This is a catastrophe for the world Socialist Revolution! She's left defenseless against four approaching carrier groups. With nothing to do but fight, it's time for the empire to strike back. Launching 3 Backfires and a Badger against the good detected TF Hammer. It's a big risk though, since there will be only 1 operations left after this strike. Thankfully, the F4s patrolling the Norwegian Sea are completely useless, allowing the strike to approach undetected. Good old American CAP was more effective though. 4 Strike fighters = 4 CAP units. Units 1 and 2 are from the Hammer carriers, 3 and 4 over from Mustang. CAP 1 (3-4-7-8, +1) puts the Badger in danger, with 2 potential hits. It saves vs one and takes a step loss after shooting. 2 (6-9-9-10) 3 hits, but, miraculously 3 saves3 (1-3-4-6, +1) kill 1 missile4 (2-2-3-7, +1) kill 4 missiles, second step loss when Badger fails saveThe fleet's 10 points of SAM eliminate 9 additional missiles, allowing 10 missiles to get through, which total 8 hits. Sov rolls 9 so gets to allocate first hit. In all, the Soviets will allocate three hits, NATO 5. At this point, I actually messed up and only applied 6 hits to the TF: The sturgeon was eliminated and US-3 took a step loss. The Soviets dreamt big and applied two hits to the Kitty Hawk, one to the Saratoga. Q: When hits are applied to a carrier, do they roll for carrier damage immediately or do they wait until all hits for the strike are allocated, thereby rolling only a single time for the carrier with +1 die for "each additional hit taken at the same time?" That's how I played it. The onslaught of Soviet air power is unrelenting. These Backfires more than earn their fearsome reputation today. We will always remember the bravery of those 6000 persons on the Kitty Hawk that day. Hawk gets 3 dice against it (2-9-0) and, with an N10 is SUNK!!! 2 dice are rolled against the Saratoga (3-7) damaging the ship. Luckily for us, no aircraft were damaged. Q: When "half of all air must roll" does NATO get to choose whether the fighters or strike craft are the ones at risk?On NATo's turn, The Saratoga joins TF Mustang, while the US 2 and 3 units join AegisQ: What is the total Ops cost for these maneuvers: 1, 2, or 3?  I played 2REPAIR: SAM loses a hitNext, Mother Bear spends their last point to put the Foxbat on patrol in the Barents sea. So, the Soviets have landed a significant blow, but have only one op left for the turn and no SAM defenses. Seeking vengence for their brothers, TF Mustang launches a strike at the Kola Airfield. All three carrier strike groups launch with fighter escorts. The Foxbat doesn't even notice them (2-3) But the CAP rolled well, causing step losses to all three fighter unit. An N10 even took a step out of the Nimitz's CAG. Still, 5 dice with no SAM protection could be rough. In total, 5 hits, 5 kills. The Foxhound was eliminated, while a Bear F and a Flogger each took a step loss. SHIPS: Both NATO TF's move into the Barents Sea. Being outclassed and needing to preserve any semblence of CAP capacty, the Soviets decline fighter-to-fighter combat and the YAK 38s are marked spent. With their last op NATO moves the Saratoga over to TF Aegis. Turn 2 The brave comrades of Kola make their desperate last stand. NATO sailors push the limits of their endurance. Running out of options, the Soviet TF launches its missiles at TF Mustang. F-14s fail to stop the missles, but Uncle Sam's SAM are brutally efficient, letting only one missile get through. It misses. Smelling Victory, Mustang launches another escorted strike. However, fatigue is clearly setting in on the carriers' beleaguered crew. Despite a total lack of resistance from Soviet defenses, they only manage to score a single hit on the ports. The Soviets are desperate to regain any semblance of functionality. They pay two points to repair a damage to the airfield and then go into the REPAIR step. SAM is down to 2 hits now, Airbase moves to Light Damage. The NATO fly boys over in England are running on fumes at this point too. Despite a wholly ineffective CAP, English Buccaneers don't manage a single hit. SHIPS: detections degrade The Victor II attacks TF Mustang dealing a step loss to US-5. It isn't enough to make a difference though. Mustang strikes again. One step of fighters is downed by CAP, leaving the Nimitz without a complement of f-14s. The CAG's free SEAD gets a hit and a roll of (3-0-0) ends the game in NATOs favor.

tier2.threadTitle: 1983 Tactical Surprise Scenario Carried Out 20th Feb at Unthril Event (Lake District)

tier2.author: Kain00
tier2.body: As per above we carried out this game. Last year at the event Jim and myself played (for 2 days) GDW "The Third World War" Full game. Therefore we'd thought about playing the naval version at the same event this turn.Pre Turn NATO:1. UK Task force (including the Royal/Dutch Marines) was formed and placed in the North Sea. 2. A couple of the subs were broken down to allow these to be placed inside the at sea convoys.3. The French Airforce was deployed in the North Sea to provide cover to the UK task force. I was worried that the UK airfields would be hit, hence was the French were used.Turn 1:NATO (Via UK Taskforce) landed troops in southern Norway and retreated back to the Atlantic before they were attacked. Although this meant they only landed 1 unit of troops I think this was a good move. The whole fleet was then able to be used to protect convoys.The French Task force protecting the convoy took a hammering and the Foch was sunk.The 4 American Carriers actually joined forces in the eastern atlantic and headed north. This meant I left the Med a bit bare of units, but I was hoping the turn 3 USA carrier reinforcements would arrive in time to help.With the help of a number of Warsaw Pact card plays, Iceland fell on turn 1 and was turned into a Soviet airbase. they also managed to land some troops in Northern NorwayLucky play of the Captor mine unit early on managed to continue to do damage to the Russian Submarine fleet. This in a way compensated for the loss of Iceland.Turn 2:Both at sea convoys managed to get into port with no damage and landed enough supplies to stop Warsaw advance both in Germany and the southern front.The German air units were sent (twice) into the Baltic to attack Russian airfields, but did not create enough damage to do any good.The combined might of USA carriers attacked Iceland and managed to take out some Soviet planes, but more importantly put heavy damage to the airfield.US and UK air attacks on a northern fleet failed to hit. This task force was probably out trying to get around northern UK to hit the US carrier group.Turn 3:The heat was being turned up by the many attacks on the US carrier group by soviet submarines. However apart from some escorts being hit, the carriers managed to stave off any damage.Carriers continued to bomb Iceland and were in a position to attack Norway.A second convoy arrived in Brest with 2 hits.The Minsk Task force was hit by US/UK submarines and most of the ships were sunk. This Task force turned around !Turn 4:US Carriers started to support the Danish position. Baltic had been cleared of NATO assets by this time and Danish airfields were badly damaged. A number of German plane units had also been destroyed.More and more Warsaw troops were being landed both in Norway and Denmark. Norway looks like they would be surrendering if no more support from the US carriers were given. However a very large convoy had been forced in the USA consisting of the UK Fleet, numerous other escorts (Including the Italian Navy) and multiply merchant ships. The Atlantic had been near enough cleared of Soviet submarines (Cuba had been left alone)We had to call it a day however.The turn 3 US Carriers were delayed slightly as I had forgotten to form a Task Force. However they were heading to the Med to support the war down there.The remaining carrier air groups would of had to continue to be used to support Denmark and as much as possible Norway. However their air units were starting to get worn down. however air reinforcements were at hand (i.e. I kept a card which would of been used to supply enough units to replace 2 carrier groups).I enjoyed the game. Pity we couldn't spend enough time to continue to completion, however as we were at a mini war game convention in the Lake District (Unthril) we had plenty of other games wanting to play. We started opening the game box at 11am and had everything tided away by 9pm. Might seem a long time but we had plenty of down time eating and talking to others at the convention.Both Jim and myself were not too familiar with the game rules. However Stuart Tonge is very active on BGG and I managed to clear up a fair few points (rule wise) before the convention.In fact I think I'm now going to set up the game in my spare table and play solo as NATO (I have downloaded Stuarts Soviet Solo Bot). We'll see how we get on...…..Super game !

tier2.body: Hello all, I finally had a chance to get back to BWN tonight. I'm loving it. Tonight, I dipped my feet into the waters of scenario 2 in order to try and get acquainted with TFs, Fighters, and the like. What follows is the AAR for the first turn. It's written more procedurally than narratively, because I want to make sure that I'm understanding all the rules. For me, this is a pretty complicated heavy game. It really flows once you get it down though, I think.  Questions are interspersed in bold. Please let me know if you see me doing anything wrong or if you know the answers to my questions. Thanks.n.b. F4 Phantom starts OP in East 3OPS: Soviet Bear MP goes On Patrol (OP) in E3. The OP Phantom attempts to intercept, rolling on the "Fighter Combat vs. Maritime Patrol" table and rolls 9, +1 for the fighter's tactical value. According to the table this results in "-1 search, per die"QUESTION: How long does this effect last for? Since I'm not presently looking to make a roll, is it a moot point?Finally, the MP goes OP and the F4 returns to base spent. SHIPS TURN: TF Black moves from Mid 5 into East 3. Soviet MP rolls detection (2-0). TF gets good detection, revealing US-5 and the convoy. MP returns to Kola spent. TF Hammer moves from the UK Port into North 3-4. A sub could then theoretically join the TF, if present. This is not possible, because the Oberon is a diesel. TF Delta moves from the UK port into East 4.QUESTION: If there is bad weather in East 4, the TF can still enter, yes? It would only need a moving marker if it began the ships step in the sea zone. Spent marker is removed from the British F4 fighter. QUESTION: IF there had been a carrier in this TF, would the Soviet MP have been intercepted when they started to return to Kola? This question is based on where it says that carrier interception occurs when an air unit exits a zone?OPS:  French Atlantique, ASW East 3 (6-0-0) BAM! Goodbye Foxtrot. Next, the other Foxtrot moves and attacks TF in East 3. 4 dice for ASuW and an additional die for good detection (1-4-5-8-8). TF ASW = 5 (4 for US-5 and 1 for the convoy), so the TF rolls 2 dice with a +1 bonus (9-0). NATO chooses to cancel 1 hit and gives 1 step loss to the Foxtrot. Convoy has 1 hit, sub is marked spent. QUESTION: Am I correct that with a 10 and an N10. I can either cancel the two hits on my TF OR give 2 step losses to the Foxtrot (defense = 9) OR 1 of each?Small moves follow: A Phantom goes OP in N3-4, Victor II OP in N5-6, UK Nimrod ASW E3 for no effect. Phantom OP in East 3. Than, Soviets launch a STRIKE against TF Black in E3. The Backfire and the Tanker take a route that traverses 5 zones. Because of the tanker, the Backfire is still at full missiles. The Phantoms intercept upon entering East 3. F4 has 3 Air-to-Air dice but are -1 die as on OP fighter, so 2 dice for NATO intercept (2-0). The N10 allows NATO to destroy 1 step of the Backfire. The fighter returns to base spent. TF has 4 points of SAM and there are 3 incoming missiles, so TF rolls 4 dice (1-1-3-7), bad luck. 1 missile gets through for a it. After rolling an N9, Soviets can allocate that hit. The convoy now has 2 hits total. The strike force returns to Kola.More OPS: British Nimrod ASW in E3. (2-5-0). Foxtrot destroyed. TU95 goes OP in N5-6. Because NATO doesn't want to leave the TF w/o fighters prior to the Ship turn, they decline to intercept the MP. SHIPS: TF Black moves to E4 and degrades to Poor Detection. TF Delta puts on a moved marker due to the weather in E4TF Hammer moves into N5-6 (also bad weather). OP Bear rolls 2d for detection (5-6). Good Detection. TF comprises UK ASW-1 and UK-AAW Non-MP air are all available again. OPS: Another STRIKE mission in E4 vs TF Black (Poor Detection). TF Delta reveals that it has a carrier and it's Sea Harriers intercept on CAP (rolls 6-9) The 6 is useless but, with the Harriers' +1 Tac Value,  the 9 becomes a 10 and will destroy the last Backfire step. Because it is not a N10, however, the missiles still launch. 4 SAM from the US-5 (2-2-4-8) 1 missile gets through (roll 5) for 1 hit. After two low dice get rolled for allocation, NATO assigns the hit to the US fleet for a step loss.Next, Nato transfers the Nimrod in the North Sea to OP in E6. Victor II fast moves from N9: N7, E9 (crossing GUIK where no is available for interception), E6.  OP Nimrod's ASW has no effect. NATO ends their turn with the Dutch Atlantique conducting ASW in N4-5 Bad weather limits the plane to 1 die, but it's a 9, for a step loss on the Victor II. With basically nothing to do, the Soviets give up their last op of the turn. I thought this scenario was a lot of fun. NATO got very lucky with their ASW rolls. In final tally, the convoy arrived with 3 hits and the amphib with only 1. NATO victory.

tier2.author: clarkcramer
tier2.body: I have to say that I am a huge fan of modern naval games and was really looking forward to this one...it seemed to be the game we have deserved on this topic for so long. I must admit that my ardor has cooled somewhat after reading the rulebook. The game is complicated and process heavy, which I appreciate, and does not put me off at all. However, the sheer number of errata, clarifications, and inconsistencies is alarming. I hesitate to be too negative, because I recognize the genius underlying the design, and also because I know that this is an ambitious project, particularly for a freshman designer. I suspect this may be why no prior games on this topic exist, even though it is long overdue. By reading through the threads, much light is shed, although the game begs for a second edition rulebook, or at least an index. For the time being, can someone please help me with the following:1)NATO boomer hunting: 23.0 says it can be earned either through spying or through the roll of a 10 with an anti-submarine warfare roll. When does this roll take place? During an anti-sub combat? Or does the Soviet player simply announce "I want the marker" and roll an anti-submarine die, hoping for a 10? If so, is this an action? The marker is then spent by rolling a 10 when resolving ASW. Again, is this any ASW combat? Say I'm attacking a Los Angeles class in the Azores, and roll a 10, I can kill a Boomer?2) US amphibious units have a helicopter symbol. Rule 14.3 explains that Amphibs don't have intrinsic detection capability. I read somewhere (I think in a thread on the geek) that the helicopter graphic represents ASW helicopters, although amphibious units have no ASW rating (my counters are cut out so its hard to evaluate each counter, but as far as I know, none do). Does the helicopter symbol have some other significance?3)US surface combatants can apparently only engage other surface units with SSMs, which, as far as I know, are all blue missiles. Although 17.14 says "white and red missiles may only be used through the play of cards," I gather (I don't remember where from) that this is true for blue missiles as well. So, let's say US surface unit 1, with a Ticonderoga, a CF Adams, and a Knox, comes across a defenseless, good detected Soviet convoy (a slow unit), delivering supplies to the Russian effort in Denmark or whatever (maybe unlikely, but let's just say). I eagerly look in my hand, and unfortunately, I have no SSM launch cards (I counted at one point, I think its on 5 of the 40 NATO cards). So my Ticonderoga, bristling with missiles, guns, torpedoes, slingshots, and god alone knows what else, sits and watches the convoy as it drifts by to deliver its precious cargo of borscht and lard to the Soviet front line? Can I at least ram them? Have I missed a rule?Please help...I am trying hard to love this game!

tier2.body: Last turn - roll for weather first:West: 3 - clear - nowhere to hide for the YankeesMid: 5 - clearEast: 1 - clearNorth - 9 - still stormy let's see where… 1, 9, 10Bad weather in the Bastion - cover for the Allied SSNs from the TF as they get their last shot…Set Soviets and US to 7 ops and the Soviets are up first. The IL38 from Kola flies to the Bastion in the midst of bad weather to help the TF ASW ops.The TF resolves its first ASW ops of the turn.2 (Krivak) + 3 (Udaloy) + 1 (Kiev) + 0 (for carrier bad weather) + 1 (IL38 Patrol bad weather) = 73 dice no modifier - 4,4,6 - gotta love those rocket torpedoes…The US selects which submarine takes the hit - one of the LAsEvasion roll - 9 - gotta love those countermeasures…The US needs to sink a Yankee SSBN per the victory conditions - and to increase the units/odds will start with the Roosevelt Roads P-3. Will the Yankees evade now, or in response to the follow on SSNs? And where should the Yankees evade to?Can't take the chance - rolling for evasion - 4. Not this time.The P-3 rolls 3 dice - 7,7,8 - and the damaged Yankee SSN is gone.Back to the Soviets. In hindsight, it's good the Yankee did not evade.The remaining Yankee SSBN puts the pedal to the metal and takes advantage of the Roosevelt Roads P-3 not being on Patrol and drives to Mid-4. This is still adjacent to a Yankee First Strike zone but out of range (SSN move 2 areas and attack or move 3 areas no attack) of the US SSNs for an attack. But still, the Yankee is still in range of the Bermuda P-3.The Bermuda P-3 goes after her…But the Yankee can roll for evasion, now it is 8+ since she is spent - 8!!The Boomer with 9 lives. And as predicted the game may have come down to an evasion roll.She has to stay adjacent to a Yankee First Strike area (Bermuda) but at least 3 spaces from the US SSNs - north off the coast of Nova Scotia works.Back to the Soviets again.With both P-3's Spent the remaining Yankee SSBN hits the accelerator and joins up off Nova Scotia.Now both Yankee SSBNs are out of attack range of the US SSNs off Jamaica…Did not expect that twist - if I understand the victory conditions correctly since both Yankee SSBNs escaped destruction it doesn't matter at this point what happens in the Bastion?Back to the US - at this point its time for the SSNs in the Bastion to start taking their shots.First LA - 2 dice +1 - 1,6 - just not enough.Back to the Soviets - even though bad weather reduces their effectiveness need to start loading up the Bastion with more MPs/Bears on Patrol first to help with the next round of TF ASW ops.Then the next LA attacks for the US - 2 dice +1 - 6, 8 - 1 hitThe Soviets choose the damaged Delta I/for the minimum payload points lost.The Soviets fly one more Bear On Patrol to get to TF ASW 3+1 dice after the US next ops.In hindsight maybe each Bear should have just attacked with 1 die and hoped for a 10, but the US would have taken the hit from the damaged LA's that have already attacked. At lease they get 2 chances - aid with TF ASW, then a later solo attack.Now the Swiftsure attacks - 2 dice +1 - 1, 4 - whiff.Since Ops in on a SHIP space time for TF resolution - the Soviet TF will conduct its second and last ASW Ops with the Patrolling MPs assistance . But the Bad weather reduces all 3 MPs to 1 ASW point and no Carrier bonus.They get 9 ASW points which translates to 3 dice +1 - 2, 7, 8 - whiff and no rockets either.Back to the Soviets for the next Ops point - the MPs will start taking their 1 die shot and returning to base.First Bear - 9 - so close.Next the last US SSN takes her shot - 2 dice +1 - 2, 2 - whiff and no US rocket torpedoes.The second Bear takes her shot - 6 - miss.Back to the US, and the long-range Nimrod in England flies to the Barents to go after the Foxtrot hopefully to prevent her from entering the Bastion.3 dice - 4, 4, 7. another miss.And the last MP in the Bastion (IL-38) - 5 - miss.With the nothing else to attack the US LA off Jamaica attacks the Yankee SSN before she can run to escort her fellow Yankees off Nova Scotia.3 dice +1 - 3, 4, 9 - 1 hit and she is damaged.The Soviet has 1 op left. Either the damaged Yankee SSN can run to safety or the Foxtrot can enter the Bastion and take one last shot at the US SSNs. Going for that last shot in the Bastion.The Foxtrot gets 2 dice - 8, 8 - bummer, she has no rocket torpedoes so a final whiff.Finally, the Sturgeon takes one last shot at the Yankee SSN3 dice +1 - 3, 4, 9 - and the Yankee SSN is gone.And that's all she wrote…US Losses - 4 damaged SSNs in the Bastion.Soviet losses:12 payload points including the damaged Yankee SSBN -  possibly subtract 2 points for the Alfa and November points that crossed the SOSUS barrier.That would still be 10 payload points which is enough for a US win but…No Yankee SSBNs were sunk so the Soviets pull a victory from the jaws of defeat.And here is what Soviet victory looks like.Hopefully this AAR was helpful in seeing the game in action.Even though this was an intro/training scenario, it begins to reveal all the decision making and trade offs that need to be considered when playing. Also, the way the systems/adjustments/procedures work it seems to 'feel' true to life - for a hypothetical conflict. Finally, being an ex-submariner from this time in history it reminds me of what could have been, but luckily for all our sakes did not happen.

The Krivak and Udaloy have rocket torpedoes allowing one die to be increased to 8 and the other discarded. Unfortunately, the Allied Subs both have a 10 defense so still no effect.Now the Allied Subs can choose between SSBNs or the TF for their attacks... Duh, go for the Boomers.Rules question - an MP on patrol supporting a TF ASW operation still stays fresh and is available for independent actions later in the turn?Since the Bastion is a dangerous place for an enemy SSN - the US for its first Ops decides to perform an ASW attack with the Sturgeon.3 Dice + 1 DRM - 2, 9, 10 - 2 10 hits.Again the Victor assisting the TF takes the first hit, and the 2nd hit finishes off the damaged Delta III for 3 more payload points.Rules Question - Subs part of a TF can still take ASW hits from enemy ASW attacks?The next Soviet Ops is spent putting a Bear from Kola On Patrol in the Bastion (instead of attacking like the last turn) in anticipation of the remaining 2 LA SSNs entering the Bastion and/or providing assistance to the 2nd SHIP event/TF ASW Op.The next US Ops is used to allow the damaged Swiftsure to perform an ASW attack in the Bastion - on the chance that the Soviets try to destroy her.She gets 2 dice w/ +1 DRM - 2, 10 - dodged the intrinsic Bastion defense and inflicting one more hit. Down goes the Victor and the Soviet SSNs have done their job - eating torpedoes for the SSBNs.Back to the Soviets - and they continue to beef up the ASW assets in the Bastion putting the last Kola based Bear On Patrol there.Back to the US. The US is going to take a chance and send the range 2 Nimrod in England to attack the Foxtrot on patrol in the Barents Sea to try to clear the way for the LA's.The Nimrod gets 3 dice - 1,6,6 - same result as the Bear last turn - whiff.And a wasted Ops point.SHIPS will occur again after the next expended Soviet and US Ops points.The Soviets go first - and honestly, they don't want to do anything but can't pass since do not have LESS Ops than the US.The SSBN's need to stay in the Bastion under protection and the Yankee SSBN's don't need to move, become spent, and reduce their chance of evading the US SSNs when they attack.I assume the Soviets can expend an Ops point but do nothing. Correct?Now the US - after the US spends an Ops the Soviet TF can perform ASW - so the US will defer sending the 2 LA's into the Bastion until after the SHIP/TF ASW action. Instead the SSNs near Cuba/S.America begin their attacks on the Yankee SSBNs.First, the Sturgeon moves to attack - both Yankee SSBN's roll for evasion - argh - 1,2 - neither evade!But neither are Spent so they can try again at 6+ for the next SSN attack.The Sturgeon attacks with 3 dice and +1 DRM - 5,7,9.All the Yankees have an 8 Defense so 2 hits - Soviets choose SSN for the first hit, then US Chooses SSBN for the second. These Sturgeons are dangerous...Now the SHIP action - TF Borodino conducts ASW Ops in the Bastion w/o the Victor but now with 3 MP's on PatrolShips get 6 + 2 Carrierx3 MPs give 9 Total 17 - 1 short again of max so get 4 dice no modifiers - 2, 6, 7, 8 - again whiff… And no rockets.Now that the TF ASW Ops are done for the turn the Soviets will use a not an action to return the patrolling IL-38 to base as Fresh and then expend an Ops Point to put it On Patrol in the Barents. This way both LA's will be interdicted as they move thru the Barents (Foxtrot/IL-38) and enter the Bastion (x2 Bears).With 3 Ops remaining the US decides to spend one more point on the Yankee Hunt before sending the 2 LA's thru the gauntlet to the Bastion.The LA north of Haiti moves into the Yankee First Strike area and they roll again for evasion - 7, 9 - this time BOTH evade and take an SSN with them. The LA just hears them go and for 2 of the Yankees, Havana so close…For the Soviets nothing to do again - most units are Spent or On Patrol and the SSBNs are not leaving the Bastion.Back to the US for the first LA run on the Bastion.In the Barents, the Foxtrot reacts - 4 dice - 4,6,7,9 - no joy.Next entry into the Bastion and 1 of the Bears - 3+1 dice - 1,1,10,10 - 2 hitsThe LA rolls for evasion - 3,6! She's damaged but makes it into the Bastion and commences its attack.The LA gets 2 dice and +1 DRM - 2,4 - fail.Perhaps she was a bit shaken up by the gauntlet she had to go thru.Per above no Soviets can or want to do anything again so the US expends the last Ops point of the turn and the 2nd LA starts her run.First, in the Barents the IL-38 takes a shot at her - 3 dice - 1,6,8 no joy.Next, the Bear as she enters the Bastion - 3+1 dice - 1,5,8,10 - 1 hit Evasion - 2Also DamagedShe gets 2 dice and +1 DRM - 5,10 - 1 hit.The Soviets pick a Delta I/II for damage - 2 Payload pointsIs there anything the Soviets could have done better?Some rules clarifications above but otherwise on to the last turn…Rules question - an MP on patrol supporting a TF ASW operation still stays fresh and is available for independent actions later in the turn?Rules Question - Subs part of a TF can still take ASW hits from enemy ASW attacks?Rules Question - I assume the Soviets can expend an Ops point but do nothing. Correct?

tier2.author: vonGekko
tier2.body: BackgroundThis is a smaller scenario focusing on NATO’s need to reinforce and resupply in the early days of the war.  The NATO player must deliver a supply convoy to France and secure the safe transit of their rapid reaction troops to reinforce Norway.  The Soviets have allocated air and sub assets to destroy these task forces before they reach their destinations. NATO Forces-US mixed surface naval group, escorting a supply convoy bound for France-UK anti-air and anti-sub surface naval groups with the carrier HMS -Illustrious and its complement of Sea Harriers, escorting an amphibious group carrying troops to reinforce Norway-A UK diesel sub group in the North Sea-UK fighter squadrons based in northern UK-Maritime patrol aircraft patrolling the North Sea and based in the UK and mainland EuropeSoviet Forces-Diesel and nuclear attack sub groups located in the mid-Atlantic and Barents Sea, respectively-Two long range naval bomber regiments and supporting maritime patrol aircraft, based at airbases on the Kola Peninsula-One spy on the spy trackVictory ConditionsThe Soviet players wins if both the convoy and the amphibious group suffer three hits each, otherwise NATO wins so long as the convoy reaches a French port and the amphibious group reaches Trondheim.Additional Rules and ConditionsThis scenario uses the Small Scenario Ops Track, with the Soviets receiving 8 OPS and NATO receiving 6 OPS each turn. Prior to beginning play, the NATO player may: deploy their UK surface units (that begin at the south UK port) into 1 or 2 task forces, ready to sailmove any 2 air units and put them on patrolPre-Game ActionsNATO’s initial concern was for the relatively isolated supply convoy and its US naval escort, designated Task Force Black.  NATO’s pre-game air unit moves were spent dispatching a UK Nimrod group and a French Atlantique group to zone East 3 to patrol ahead of TF Black’s course, ready to rendezvous after the first ship move.The UK surface groups, HMS Illustrious, and the amphibious group were formed up at Portsmouth as Task Force Shield.I opted to roll for weather for the relevant Sea Zones as part of the setup, resulting in the placement of a Bad Weather marker in zone East 6.Initial LocationsTURN 1Soviet OPS (8 --> 7)The hunt for the NATO supply convoy begins, with a Bear-D unit from Kola sent along a northerly route to zone East 3, initiating a patrol in the hopes of sighting the convoy as soon as it moves.Ships MovementTime is of the essence, forcing NATO to use the most direct routes.  TF Shield sorties from Portsmouth into the North Sea (North 3-4).  As part of the TF’s movement, it is joined by the Oberon class diesel group to bolster its ASW defense. EDIT: As noted in a post by another player, this joining move is not valid.  The Oberon is a diesel sub and only nuclear subs may join a TF.TF Black moves into zone East 3.  The Bear-D group patrolling in the zone has been waiting and attempts to locate them.  The Bear-D rolls its 2 search dice, resulting in 1 - 9, allowing a Good Detection marker to be placed on TF Black. It’s mission complete, the Bear-D group turns North towards home.The Bear-D is returned to its airbase and marked Spent.NATO OPS (6 --> 5)In anticipation of a possible Soviet air strike, a group of UK F-4 Phantoms is tasked to patrol zone East 3 over TF Black.Soviet OPS (7-->6)Soviet sub groups near TF Black have its location.  They move in to attack.The Foxtrot in zone Mid 5 moves into East 3 to attack TF Black.   The Nimrod and Atlantique groups pick up a possible new submerged contact.  They alert the commander of TF Black and request permission to break their patrols and aggressively work this contact.  The commander is concerned there may be more subs out there and he doesn’t want to expend his critical ASW assets this early.  He tells both the ASW aircraft to maintain their patrols and coordinate with the TF ships as part of an organized ASW defense.The NATO player chooses not to trigger individual ASW attacks from the MP aircraft, opting to fold their bonuses into the Task Force ASW defense rolls.The soviet subs maneuver for position and attack the task force with torpedoes.The Foxtrot group rolls its 4 surface attack dice plus an additional die for the Good Contact established on the TF, resulting in 3-4-5-7-9.  The 7 and 9 results would normally each result in a hit on a non-capital ship.The TF ships and aircraft overhead work to foil the attacking subs. The task force ASW total, including the supporting MP aircraft is 4+1+3+3=11.  This provides 3 ASW dice and a +1 tactical value.  The TF rolls 4-6-6, effectively 5-7-7 with the tactical bonus.  Normally this would be an ineffective result, however the TF rolled a double result and one of the constituent ship groups is armed with rocket torpedoes.  With this weapon system type, any double result can be changed to a single 8 result which cancels a hit rolled in the sub attack.  Thus, the TF ASW defense effectively reduces the hits on the TF from 2 to 1.The Soviet subs, frustrated by aggressive ASW defenses, manage only a single hit which they assign to the convoy.The attacking Foxtrot group is now marked Spent.NATO OPS (5 --> 4)Air cover over TF Shield is bolstered by the assignment of a group of UK F-4 Phantoms into the North Sea, zone North 3-4.Soviet OPS (6-->5)The second Soviet sub group near TF Black has received a communication from Red Fleet HQ.  “Initial attack results undesirable. To fail again means to waste ourselves and to waste at the same time our Motherland.”The Soviet sub group commits to its fate and attacks TF Black.The Foxtrot group rolls its 4 surface attack dice plus an additional die for the Good Contact established on the TF, resulting in 2-4-9-10-10.  The 9 would normally result in a hit on a non-capital ship, the natural 10 results may be used to hit any ship and one of the 10’s can be used to apply 2 hits on a convoy. Against this devastating attack, TF ships and aircraft scramble to counter. As before, the task force ASW total is 4+1+3+3=11 for 3 ASW dice and +1 tactical value.  The TF rolls 2-5-9, effectively 3-6-10.   The 10 result is enough to reduce the attacking sub (flipped to damaged side) AND remove one of the sub group’s rolled hits.  The Soviets pay with the losses but succeed in a crippling attack, delivering two hits to the convoy (from the 10 result) and damaging the US surface group (with the 9 result). The attacking Foxtrot group is now marked Spent.The results of the Foxtrot group attacks NATO OPS (4 --> 3)NATO forces in the North Sea, zone North 3-4, are joined by an Atlantique from the Netherlands. Soviet OPS (5-->4)The Soviets have ravaged the convoy and weakened TF Black’s defences.  A follow up air strike could reap further rewards, but at this range could only include T-22M Backfires operating with reduced missile loads.  If the closer NATO amphibious group could be located, the full weight of both available bomber regiments could be brought to bear.The remaining Bear-D unit from Kola is sent down the Norwegian coast into the North Sea on a hazardous mission to locate TF Shield.  The clouds over the North Sea hide RAF F-4 Phantoms and Sea Harriers from the Illustrious, all prowling for intruders. The UK F-4 Phantom rolls 3-2=1 die for Fighter vs. MP aircraft.  The result is 4, adjusted to 5 by the Phantom’s tactical value.  This has no effect.  The Sea Harriers on CAP roll 2-2=0, but can roll a minimum of 1 die.  The result is also a 4, adjusted to 5 by the Sea Harrier’s tactical value.  Again, no effect.Sweating bullets, the Bear-D group begins its patrol pattern in the hopes of spotting the surface group.  The Bear-D rolls its 2 search dice, resulting in 2 - 10, allowing a Good Detection marker to be placed on TF Shield.  After relaying the coordinates, the Bear-D doesn’t wait for confirmation, hurriedly turning back to base.  The Bear-D unit is returned to its airbase and marked Spent.TF Shield in the North SeaSoviet OPS (4-->3)The naval aviation bombers have been waiting at ready status for this moment.  Two regiments rise from the Kola airfields and head for the coordinates relayed by their comrades. EDIT: As noted in a post by another player, the OPS cost for this strike should be TWO, one for each regiment participating. The previously played Move and Patrol OPS resulted in a detection, allowing the phasing player to immediately pay an additional OPS for an action that will result in an attack on the spotted target.Upon arrival in the North Sea target zone, the strike is intercepted by the UK F-4 Phantom unit.The Phantoms attack the Backfires.  They have 3 Air Attack dice, minus 1 die for being the intercepting unit.  They roll 5 - 7, adjusted by the Phantoms tactical value to 6 - 8.  The results are neither enough to reduce the bomber group or fulfill the criteria for detecting the raid.  The Sea Harriers on CAP are next to engage.The Sea Harriers also attack the Backfires.  They have 2 Air Attack dice, with no penalties or bonuses.  They roll 1 - 8, adjusted by their tactical value to 2-9.  The results are still not enough to reduce the bomber group. Despite the best efforts by the TF air cover, the full force of the bomber strike is unleashed as missiles streak towards their targets.  The Backfires, at normal range, contribute 6 missiles while the Badgers, at extended range, contribute 3.  A total of 9 missiles are on the missile track.  The TF anti-air defenses spring into action, missiles leaping from their rails into the sky.  The TF rolls 1+4+1=6 dice total, with results of 1-3-4-6-6-10.  This results in 6 hits, leaving 3 incoming missiles to resolve on the Incoming Missile Resolution Table.  For the first pair, a roll of 3 indicates 1 hit.  For the remaining missile, a roll of 10 indicates another hit. The subsequent hit allocation die roll (a 6 - 7) allows the NATO player to allocate both hits and these are allocated to the Illustrious and the ASW group.  Both are flipped to their reduced sides and the Sea Harrier air group is reduced.While the Royal Navy’s air defenses performed admirably, destroying many of the incoming missiles, the carrier force has been dealt a major blow, and several other ships have been stricken.  Nonetheless, the amphibious ships weathered the attacks without loss, much to the relief of the brave soldiers within their hulls.With the strike completely resolved, the Backfire and Badger units are returned to their airbase and both marked Spent.TF Shield's ships following the 1st Turn air strikeShips MovementTF Black moves into the Bay of Biscay, zone East 4, along with its attendant maritime patrol craft and fighter cover. The detection level on the TF is degraded to Poor Detection.  TF Shield moves into the Norwegian Sea, zone North 5-6, along with its attendant maritime patrol craft and fighter cover.  The detection level on the TF is degraded to Poor Detection.  Each TF is now within one movement of its final objective port.EDIT: As noted in a post by another player, this phase should also have included removing Spent markers from non-MP aircraft units at base.  Consequently, the Backfire group at Kola should have been available for another strike this turn.NATO OPS (3-->2)The NATO commander knows there are no immediate threats to TF Black remaining for this turn, whereas TF Shield will likely be facing imminent sub attack.  Consequently, he recalls the Nimrod group protecting TF Black and dispatches it to the Norwegian Sea, zone North 5-6, to strengthen TF Shield’s ASW component.Soviet OPS (3-->2)With precious little time and operations left, the Soviet player knows his attack subs in the Barents Sea are his last best weapon to stop the amphibious group.  One of the two Victor II units is ordered into the Norwegian Sea to conduct an attack on TF Shield.  The sub rolls its 2 surface attack dice, resulting in 1-8.  The 8 would normally result in a hit on a non-capital ship.Even in its damaged state, TF Shield’s ASW defenses are formidable and the search for the attackers commences.  The task force ASW total is 2+1+2+9+3+3+3=23, maxing out the ASW table to 4 dice and +1 tactical value.  The TF rolls 4+4+5+6.  Even with the tactical bonus, the rolls aren’t impressive, however the double result can trigger the UK ASW group’s rocket torpedo ability to create an 8 result - enough to negate the sub group’s only hit. The sub group is marked Spent.  Although the sub group escapes unscathed, its attack is ineffective.NATO OPS (2 --> 1)The remaining F-4 Phantom unit at the north UK Air Base is sent to fly cover over TF Shield in the North Sea, zone North 3-4.Soviet OPS (2-->1)The remaining Victor II unit is ordered into the Norwegian Sea to conduct an attack on TF Shield.  This time, the NATO commander feels he has the ASW coverage to spare an active attack on the sub as it enters the zone.  The Dutch Atlantique is given the order to prosecute the new contact. The Atlantique rolls its 3 ASW die for results 1-5-9.  The 9 result is considered a hit and the Victor II group is reduced. The Atlantique is successful in its attacks and returns to Amsterdam to rearm.The Atlantique group is returned to the Amsterdam air base and marked Spent.  A weakened and shaken Victor II group attempts to press home an attack on the task force.  The sub rolls 1 surface attack die, resulting an 8.  The 8 would normally result in a hit on a non-capital ship.  TF Shield’s ASW defenses respond immediately.  The sub group is hounded by air and surface groups alike.  The task force ASW total is 2+1+2+9+3+3=20, maxing out the ASW table to 4 dice and +1 tactical value.  The TF rolls 4+5+5+8.  With the tactical bonus, the results include a nine and a rocket torpedo activation from the double result.  Both are enough to negate the sub’s hit and the 9 is another hit on the sub group, eliminating it.Soviet HQ can only speculate on the outcome of the attack as they hear no further communications from their second sub group.NATO OPS (1 --> 0)The NATO player has no additional available assets to deploy or actions to take.Soviet OPS (1-->0)The Soviet player has no additional available assets to deploy or actions to take. END OF TURN 1-All Spent markers are removed-Weather markers are removed and weather for the next turn is determined.  Weather is determined as clear for all east and north zones - no bad weather markers are placed.-The turn marker is moved to Turn 2-On the Small Scenario Ops Track, the Soviets are reset to 8 OPS and NATO reset to 6 OPS. End of Turn 1TURN 2Soviet OPS (8 --> 7)With both NATO task forces poised to enter their respective ports there is one last chance for the Soviets to deliver a decisive blow. Once again the large naval bomber formations assemble over the Kola Peninsula and head southwest to attack TF Shield. In the frigid clear skies of the Norwegian Sea, the strike is intercepted by a UK F-4 Phantom unit that bores down on the bombers.The first Phantoms attack the Backfires.  They have 3 Air Attack dice, minus 1 die for being the intercepting unit.  They roll 1 - 5, adjusted by their tactical value to 2 - 6.  The results are neither enough to reduce the bomber group or fulfill the criteria for detecting the raid.  The second Phantoms attack the Badgers.  They have 3 Air Attack dice. They roll 1- 4 - 7, adjusted by tactical value to 2 - 5 - 8.  The 8 is enough to hit the Badger, reducing it.  The strike is also now considered detected.  Cheers erupt over the radio as the fighters send multiple Badgers spiraling into the sea.  A handful of Sea Harriers on CAP are now the sole airborne defense.The reduced Sea Harrier group attacks the Badgers.  They have 1 Air Attack die, with -1 penalty for being based on a damaged carrier, but a +1 bonus for attacking a detected air strike.  They roll 8, adjusted by their tactical value to 9.  The Badger group attempts a saving roll, with a result of one.  The Badger group is now eliminated, although they still contribute their reduced missile load to the attack.  The Sea Harrier pilots exact revenge for their carrier group as they ravage the remaining Badgers, however the bombers still manage many missiles launches before they tumble from the sky.Although the TF air cover can claim many victories, a large volley of missiles are still hurtling towards the ships.  Both bomber groups are considered normal range.  The Backfires contribute 6 missiles while the reduced Badgers contribute 3.  A total of 9 missiles are on the missile track.  The task forces own missiles roar upwards to meet them.  The TF rolls 0+4+1=5 dice total, with results of 3 - 3 - 8 - 8 - 10.  This results in 6 hits, leaving 3 incoming missiles to resolve on the Incoming Missile Resolution Table.  For the first pair, a roll of 3 indicates 1 hit.  For the remaining missile, a roll of 4 indicates another hit. The subsequent hit allocation die roll (a 2 - 2) allows the NATO player to allocate both hits and these are allocated to the AAW group and the amphibious group.  The AAW group is flipped to its reduced side and the amphibious group is assigned one hit.Most of the missiles have been destroyed by the Royal Navy’s air defenses but those remaining take their toll.  Several of the British air defense destroyers have been hit and even the amphibious ships have not escaped unscathed.  Several transports are burning and others have disappeared in explosions that leave nothing behind but churning waters.With the strike completely resolved, the surviving Backfire unit is returned to its airbase and marked Spent. Ships MovementThe battered remnants of TF Black enter the port of Brest.  The dock workers note the mangled superstructures and count the incoming cargo ships, asking “Est-ce tout ce qui reste?”TF Black moves from Bay of Biscay zone East 4 into the port at Brest.  At Trondheim, a thin ring of Royal Navy destroyers and frigates form a cordon and shephard the landing ships and transports to the docks where they disembark.  Although they’ve suffered some losses, most of this mix of German and British troops have arrived safely, and will soon join their Norwegian allies at the front.   TF Shield moves from Norwegian Sea zone North 5-6 into Trondheim.SCENARIO ENDThe NATO player has met their win criteria by delivering both convoys to their destinations.  While the Soviets inflicted heavy losses, they failed to deal 3 damage to both convoys, succeeding only in with the supply convoy.   End gamePersonal OpinionsThis scenario was a lot of fun, giving me a small but interesting mix of units to learn the basics of sub combat, ASW defense, interception, and air strikes.I particularly enjoyed the sub/ASW aspect, especially the choice of whether to spend a maritime patrol aircraft’s operations on attacking a sub or keeping it on patrol to bolster TF defenses.I think this may be a challenging scenario for the Soviet player.  The NATO player can deliver both convoys to port in 3 movements, which may be accomplished in just a little over one turn.   That allows for one attack from all Soviet assets in turn 1 and one additional attack in turn 2 before the 3rd Ship Movement is triggered.Soviet naval bomber attacks are deadly, and Backfires are tough to kill.DisclaimerI’m still rather new to this system.  There are likely to be a few mistakes I made in the course of this session.  I welcome any corrections of errors I may have committed with the rules and appreciate any feedback.

tier2.author: acb3
tier2.body: Stuart Tonge  @stuuk Hello, looks mostly good - you have the mechanics all down.Two small items:Scenario rules:"NATO wins the game by sinking an SSBN payload value of 8.The Soviet player may reduce the current Payload value sunk byone for each Soviet submarine step that makes it over the SOSUSline"Since at the start of the scenario, the payload sunk is 0, you cannot do this right away - the intent is no negative numbers. However, I would just play on and know for the future.Rules:"the MP limitation of Natural 10's to hit a nuclear submarine.."I think you are confusing this with the (N) symbology - which means not magnetic, it doesn't mean nuclear.Great AAR - please keep it going!StuSo the payload/VP calculation is a running total NOT calculated at the end of the scenario? This means the Soviets should not run the SOSUS barrier until AFTER the US sinks an SSBN. And therefore the US player should focus first on sinking the Alfa/November before starting the SSBN attacks to prevent the Soviets from gaining points. The only Soviet response is to return to safer waters and/or reinforce the Bastion instead of risking destruction.As for my N confusion - Non-Magnetic makes more sense than all Nucs. One of the primary sensors on an ASW patrol aircraft is the Magnetic Anamoly Detector (MAD).Thanks for the feedback, more to come.

In step 4 if you have rolled at least a double 6 then you may convert those two dice to an instant hit IF your sub is equipped with SSM weapons. These two die rolls are now discarded and of course if you roll a double that is 7 or higher you do the other stuff. The problem is that according to the rules it says that you cause an immediate step loss if you roll a double 1-6.Also I guess that you dont actually do an SSM attack 17.13 since you could then end up doing another torpedo attack and so on  Stuart Tonge  @stuuk In terms of SAM defence, if there are more attacking missiles than defending SAMs then you are in trouble. If there are double the number, you're almost certain to take some serious damage - your ability to shoot down the incoming missiles is being overwhelmed (and at that point hiding is your only real defence).Yep I get that, I was mainly testing what would happen and how easy it is to sink carriers  The thing about carriers and hits I wondered about is as follows. Or do you first need a hit to flip the counter and then another to maybe sink it?And also thanks for a very interesting game
